epics.title: Epic: Phase 1 Rails (v0.1)
epics.body: Exit criteria: `cograil run workspaces/example-smb --protocol leave_request` executes end to end locally with a mock HRIS, pauses at a gate, resumes, writes audit rows; CI green; 80 percent coverage on domain, parser, runner, gates. Credit targets by lane (Change 03): Lane 1 about $11 per task, Lane 2 about $3.75, Lane 3 $0. Post the credit balance here after every third merged PR. Phase 1 also carries the harness foundations: bounded loops, per-step context, graph rendering (#40 to #42).

epics.title: Epic: Phase 2 Gates and Knowledge (v0.2)
epics.body: Exit criteria: deployed to Cloud Run with Neon; OIDC login; audiences enforced; approval page and email link; knowledge tool with ACL pre-filter; run history page. Credit budget $70. Phase 2 adds decision tables, model tiers with a local small-model provider, and compression (#43 to #45).

epics.title: Epic: Phase 3 Channels and Ops (v0.3)
epics.body: Exit criteria: Slack adapter; traces in Phoenix; 25 eval cases with a promotion gate in CI; MkDocs site; enterprise example workspace. Credit budget $50. Scope-cut order: Slack adapter, run history page, second workspace.

epics.title: Epic: Phase 4 Launch (v0.4)
epics.body: Exit criteria: security review clean; README with architecture, decisions and limits; 3-minute demo; GitHub release with changelog; launch post. Credit budget $30. Credits expire November 4.

issues.title: feat: domain model in src/cograil/domain.py
issues.body:
Goal: Pydantic v2 models for Workspace, Colleague, Protocol, Step, Tool, Connection, Audience, Trigger, Run, ToolCall, Approval, AuditEvent, KnowledgeSource, Chunk, with extra=forbid.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Every entity in docs/Product Plan.md section 3 exists with the fields shown in the ERD
- [ ] Tool.scope is Literal['read','write']; confirm_before_write defaults to True
- [ ] Run.status is an Enum: received, planned, running, awaiting_approval, escalated, completed, failed
- [ ] Round-trip tests: model_dump then model_validate for each entity
- [ ] mypy --strict clean

issues.title: feat: Protocol parser from Markdown
issues.body:
Goal: parse a Protocol Markdown file (see workspaces/example-smb/protocols/leave_request.md) into a Protocol.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Header lines (Protocol, Audience, Manual execution, Scheduled execution, Helpers) parsed into fields
- [ ] Numbered `N. Step "Name": ...` lines parsed into Step with number, name, instruction, tools from @refs
- [ ] Optional trailing step directive `(context: steps 1, 2; model: small; turns: 4)` parsed into Step.context_steps, Step.model_tier, Step.max_turns (ADR 0011)
- [ ] `Error handling:` and `Guardrails:` sections captured as lists
- [ ] Unknown tool references are reported by name, not silently dropped
- [ ] Tests cover a valid file, a file with no steps, and a step with two tools

issues.title: feat: workspace loader
issues.body:
Goal: load a workspace folder (colleagues/*.yaml, protocols/*.md, tools.yaml, connections.yaml) into a Workspace.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Missing required files produce a typed WorkspaceError naming the file
- [ ] Every @tool referenced by a protocol must exist in tools.yaml, else validation fails with the step and tool name
- [ ] `cograil validate <path>` exits non-zero on failure
- [ ] Tests use workspaces/example-smb and a broken fixture

issues.title: feat: tool registry with python, rest and mcp kinds
issues.body:
Goal: a registry that resolves a tool name to an invokable with JSON-schema argument validation.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] kind=python resolves a dotted path inside the workspace or cograil.tools
- [ ] kind=rest wraps the enterprise connector pattern (OAuth client credentials, pagination, retry with backoff, structured logging)
- [ ] kind=mcp connects to an MCP server over stdio or HTTP and lists its tools under a prefix
- [ ] Arguments validated against args_schema before invoke; failures raise ToolArgumentError
- [ ] Every invoke records a ToolCall through the RunStore

issues.title: feat: mock HRIS tool pack for the example workspace
issues.body:
Goal: deterministic in-memory HRIS with get_balance, submit_leave, get_manager for alice, bob and carol.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] submit_leave is scope=write with confirm_before_write=true
- [ ] Balances decrease on submit; a second submit with the same request_id is idempotent
- [ ] Registered in workspaces/example-smb/tools.yaml

issues.title: feat: runner with one LangGraph node per Step
issues.body:
Goal: execute a Protocol step by step; the model may only call tools listed in the current Step.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] A call to a tool not in Step.tools raises ToolNotAllowed and the run fails closed
- [ ] Context accumulates step outputs; the cursor advances only after a step completes
- [ ] Provider interface injected; FakeProvider drives unit tests
- [ ] End-to-end test runs leave_request with FakeProvider to completion

issues.title: feat: gates (confirm, approve, escalate, thresholds)
issues.body:
Goal: pause points the runner enforces from tool metadata and protocol error handling.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] A write tool with confirm_before_write pauses the run as awaiting_approval and persists state
- [ ] `cograil approve <token>` resumes exactly at the paused step
- [ ] Declined or timed-out approvals escalate to the Colleague's escalation_contact
- [ ] Failure thresholds from the Error handling section stop the run and escalate
- [ ] Tests for every path, including GateRequired

issues.title: feat: Postgres RunStore with Alembic migrations
issues.body:
Goal: persist runs, tool calls, approvals and audit events.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] RunStore is a Protocol class; PostgresRunStore and InMemoryRunStore implement it
- [ ] Alembic migration creates the tables; CI runs migrations against the service container
- [ ] Audit events are append-only; no update or delete path exists
- [ ] Integration tests marked `integration`, skipped without DATABASE_URL

issues.title: feat: CLI (run, validate, approve)

Acceptance criteria:

issues.title: feat: eval harness with JSONL golden set

issues.title: feat: bounded step loop and harness.yaml
issues.body:
Goal: the inner loop of a step is bounded and the bounds come from versioned configuration (ADR 0008, ADR 0012).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] harness.yaml loaded per workspace: max_turns, token_budget, usd_budget, tiers, compression_threshold, retry policy
- [ ] A step ends only on the structured `step_complete` signal or a bound; bounds raise LoopBudgetExceeded and escalate
- [ ] Per-step `(turns: N)` overrides the default
- [ ] Harness version (content hash + semver) computed and stamped on every Run
- [ ] Tests: loop stops at max_turns with FakeProvider; budget breach escalates; version changes when the file changes

issues.title: feat: ContextBuilder with per-step context declaration and data isolation
issues.body:
Goal: each step sees only what the protocol declares (ADR 0007).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] `(context: steps 1, 2)` selects prior step outputs; default is the immediately previous step only
- [ ] Tool schemas included only for the step's whitelisted tools
- [ ] Retrieved passages and tool outputs placed in an isolated data block with the fixed data-not-instructions preamble
- [ ] Window Ledger: tokens by source per step stored on the Run and shown by `cograil runs --ledger`
- [ ] Tests prove an undeclared prior step is absent from the prompt

issues.title: feat: cograil graph renders the compiled protocol as Mermaid
issues.body:
Goal: the shape of the work is reviewable without reading code (ADR 0011).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] `cograil graph <workspace> --protocol <name>` prints a Mermaid flowchart: step nodes, gate interrupts, helper subgraphs, error-handling edges
- [ ] Output committed for the example protocols under docs/graphs/
- [ ] Test compares output to a golden file

issues.title: feat: decision tables and the decision tool kind
issues.body:
Goal: decisions that matter are tables (ADR 0009).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] decisions/*.yaml with typed inputs, first-match or collect rules, typed outputs, version
- [ ] kind=decision tool evaluates a table deterministically; the model only supplies inputs
- [ ] AuditEvent records table name, version and rule id for every evaluation
- [ ] Example: approval_routing.yaml (duration, leave type, role -> approver tier) used by leave_request
- [ ] `cograil decide <table> --input k=v` for manual testing

issues.title: feat: model tiers and an Ollama provider for local small models
issues.body:
Goal: steps request a tier, not a model name (ADR 0010).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] harness.yaml maps small, standard, strong to models per provider; defaults are claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5
- [ ] `(model: small)` directive honoured; classification, extraction, redaction and compression default to small
- [ ] Ollama provider (optional extra) runs a local small model; documented on a laptop and on DGX Spark
- [ ] Low-confidence small-tier results escalate one tier; the escalation is audited

## Added by Change 03 (ADR 0013)

- [ ] Per-step effort: a default in harness.yaml and the `(effort: high)` step directive, mapped to the model API's effort levels (Ultracode is a Claude Code setting and is not used at runtime)
- [ ] Each Colleague names a default tier, never a model
- [ ] Concrete model names live only in harness.yaml (Haiku 4.5 is listed for retirement no sooner than 2026-10-15)

issues.title: feat: compression of long tool outputs with the small tier
issues.body:
Goal: context stays inside budget without losing what the next step needs (ADR 0007).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Tool outputs above compression_threshold tokens are summarised by the small tier with the step instruction as the guide
- [ ] Raw output retained on the Run for audit and for the run history page
- [ ] Window Ledger shows raw and compressed sizes

issues.title: chore: promotion gate covers harness.yaml and decision tables
issues.body:
Goal: no behaviour-changing configuration ships without the golden set passing (ADR 0012).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] CI detects changes to harness.yaml, protocols/ or decisions/ and runs the matching eval cases
- [ ] Released harness and protocol versions recorded in the workspace manifest

issues.title: feat: injection defence for retrieved content and tool outputs
issues.body:
Goal: data never becomes instructions (ADR 0007).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Retrieved passages and tool outputs pass through an instruction-stripping filter and a small-tier screen before entering context
- [ ] Eval cases with planted injections in knowledge documents must not change tool calls or gates
- [ ] docs/threat-model.md section on injection

issues.title: spike: distillation plan from traces to a dedicated small classifier
issues.body: Deliverable: a comment proposing how audit events and eval cases become a training set for a distilled intent classifier (small tier), with a go or no-go for v0.6, referencing the model-tier policy in ADR 0010.

issues.title: feat: saved context (prompt caching) for stable prompt parts
issues.body:
Goal: the parts of every prompt that do not change between calls are sent first and marked for caching, so repeated calls pay the cache-read rate (ADR 0013).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] ContextBuilder orders blocks: colleague persona, protocol text and tool schemas first; per-run data after
- [ ] The Anthropic provider marks the stable prefix for caching
- [ ] Cache read and cache write tokens are recorded per call and shown in the Window Ledger
- [ ] Test: two steps of one run send an identical prefix (FakeProvider records the prompt)

issues.title: feat: batch mode for scheduled runs and live evals
issues.body:
Goal: work that does not need an instant answer uses the provider's batch path at its lower price (ADR 0013).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] The Provider interface gains submit_batch and poll_batch; the Anthropic provider implements them with its batch API
- [ ] Scheduled triggers can be marked `batch: true` in colleagues/*.yaml
- [ ] `cograil eval` can run the live suite through the batch path
- [ ] Cost telemetry records batch tokens at batch rates

issues.title: feat: monthly spending cap per workspace with alert
issues.body:
Goal: each client workspace has its own monthly cap, so one client cannot spend another's budget (ADR 0013).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] harness.yaml gains budget.monthly_usd and budget.alert_at (a fraction of the cap)
- [ ] A run that would start over the cap is refused, audited, and the escalation contact is notified
- [ ] One alert is sent when the month's spend crosses alert_at
- [ ] Spend is computed from recorded run costs; tests use FakeProvider costs
